title: StrippedFiles
description: A stripper's answer, on stdout: the rewritten sources as data, plus which checks it actually touched. CORE writes the files, exactly as it does for an emitter — that keeps the write path, the path-escape rejection, and the dry-run in one place, and denies an adapter the ability to scribble outside the files it was asked about. A stripper reports what it changed; it never decides what should change.

generated_by.description: Adapter name and version — names the stripper for anyone reading an error that quotes it.

files.description: Every source the strip changed, with its full new content. A file whose content would be unchanged MUST be omitted, so the count core reports is the count of real edits.

path.description: Consumer-root-relative, '/'-separated, normalized. Core rejects absolute paths and any '..' segment before writing — a stripper edits the files it was handed, nothing else.

stripped.description: The check ids whose annotations changed. Core requires this to be a subset of the request: a stripper that reports touching a check nobody asked about has exceeded its instruction, and core says so rather than writing the result.
